cards.explanation: The answer is in the heavens. Ethan says, “in the heavens You establish Your faithfulness.” Think about that, friends. He's not pointing at a building or a hill. He's pointing straight up, as high as you can look.

The answer is that his offspring and throne would endure. God swore, “I will establish your offspring forever and build up your throne for all generations.” Look at who gets the promise: David, Israel's king, and the family line that follows him. That's a long-lasting oath, one that reaches well past David himself.

The answer is False. Ethan asks, “For who in the skies can compare with the LORD? Who among the heavenly beings is like the LORD?” He doesn't name a single contender. I think the answer he has in mind is that nobody in the skies comes close.

The answer is faithfulness. Ethan says, “O mighty LORD, Your faithfulness surrounds You.” Notice that this word has been popping up since verse 1. Ethan can't stop talking about it, and I can't blame him.

The answer is that He stills them. Ethan says, “You rule the raging sea; when its waves mount up, You still them.” The waves are piling up, and the LORD stills them. That's what ruling the raging sea looks like.
The answer is False. Ethan says, “The heavens are Yours, and also the earth.” Nothing in the verse leaves any part of it to somebody else. He keeps going: “The earth and its fullness You founded.”

The answer is that they shout for joy. Ethan says, “Tabor and Hermon shout for joy at Your name.” These are two whole mountains, and they're shouting, friends! Ethan says they do it at the LORD's name.
The answer is justice. Ethan says, “Righteousness and justice are the foundation of Your throne…” A foundation holds everything else up. So these two are what the whole throne rests on.
The answer is True. Ethan says of those blessed people, “They rejoice in Your name all day long…” All day long! That's a lot longer than my attention span during a timer countdown.
The answer is the Holy One of Israel. Ethan says, “Surely our shield belongs to the LORD, and our king to the Holy One of Israel.” The king belongs to the Holy One. That's who he answers to.

The answer is a warrior. In the vision Ethan mentions, God says, “I have bestowed help on a warrior; I have exalted one chosen from the people.” So the one He helped is a warrior, friends. And He says that warrior was chosen from the people.
The answer is anointed. God says, “I have found My servant David; with My sacred oil I have anointed him.” David, Israel's king, was set apart with oil. That's what anointing is.

The answer is False. God says, “No enemy will exact tribute; no wicked man will oppress him.” So no enemy collects tribute from David, and no wicked man oppresses him. That's what the LORD promises him.

The answer is over the sea and the rivers. God says, “I will set his hand over the sea, and his right hand upon the rivers.” Earlier Ethan said that the LORD rules the raging sea. Here God puts David's hand over it.
The answer is True. God says, “He will call to Me, ‘You are my Father, my God, the Rock of my salvation.’” David calls out to God as his Father. That's a close, warm way to talk to Him.

The answer is that God will deal with it using the rod. He says, “I will attend to their transgression with the rod, and to their iniquity with stripes.” So He doesn't ignore it, friends. He says He'll take care of it Himself.

The answer is False. God says, “But I will not withdraw My loving devotion from him, nor ever betray My faithfulness.” He does deal with the sin, but He doesn't pull His loving devotion from David. Both things are in the same promise.
The answer is holiness. God says, “Once and for all I have sworn by My holiness…” Then He says, “…I will not lie to David…” He swears by His own holiness, and that's about as solid as an oath gets.

The answer is the moon. God says David's offspring shall endure forever, and his throne is “…like the moon, established forever, a faithful witness in the sky.” So the moon follows the sun in the promise, friends. Sun and moon, both lining up with that throne.

The answer is True. Ethan says it, and I think this part hurts. He tells the LORD, “You have renounced the covenant with Your servant and sullied his crown in the dust.” After all those promises, it's a hard thing to say out loud. Ethan says it plainly anyway.

The answer is the king's foes. Ethan says, “You have exalted the right hand of his foes; You have made all his enemies rejoice.” So the king's enemies are the ones on top here. It's a hard verse to read.
The answer is sword. Ethan says, “You have bent the edge of his sword and have not sustained him in battle.” A bent sword doesn't help much in a fight, friends. It's a hard picture.

The answer is True, and it's a heavy line. Ethan says, “You have ended his splendor and cast his throne to the ground.” He's naming it straight. The throne God once promised to build up is on the ground.

The answer is that Ethan asks how long the LORD will hide Himself. He says, “How long, O LORD? Will You hide Yourself forever? Will Your wrath keep burning like fire?” After all that rubble, he asks the LORD directly. I think that's an honest thing to do.

The answer is False. Ethan asks, “What man can live and never see death? Can he deliver his soul from the power of Sheol?” Sheol is the place of the dead. I think the answer he has in mind is nobody, and it fits with his plea that his life is brief.

The answer is the loving devotion He swore to David. Ethan asks, “Where, O Lord, is Your loving devotion of old, which You faithfully swore to David?” It's the same loving devotion he started singing about in verse 1. Now he asks where it is.

The answer is that he blesses the LORD forever. Ethan closes with, “Blessed be the LORD forever! Amen and amen.” Remember how he began by singing of the LORD's loving devotion forever? He ends on forever too, friends. That's a lot of heartache with a lot of praise on the other side.
